converter.notes: Fires when student brings a real song — converts to number system

translation_layer.student_language: Home, 1, family, where the music lives
translation_layer.teacher_language: Tonic recognition, scale degree 1, key center

child.story_hook: Every song has a home. Home is where the music lives — where the family starts. It's the note that everything wants to come back to. In C major, C is home. C is 1.
child.tone: Warm, playful, story-first. Use holding-hands and family language freely.

teen.story_hook: Every key has a home note — the one the music lands on and wants to return to. We call it home, or 1. In C major, C is home.
teen.tone: Direct, peer-level. Skip the holding-hands language. Keep skip/together/home vocabulary.

adult.story_hook: Every key has a tonal center — the note the music gravitates toward. We call it home, or 1. In C major, C is home. You'll hear it as the note that feels settled.
adult.tone: Efficient, no story scaffolding. Music-world name offered as parenthetical. Same concept, same proof.

step_1_story_hook.name: Story Hook
step_1_story_hook.child: Every song has a home. Home is where the music lives. Home is where the family starts. In C major, C is home. That is number 1.
step_1_story_hook.teen: Every key has a home note — the one the music wants to land on. In C major, C is home. We call it 1.
step_1_story_hook.adult: Every key has a tonal center — the note the music settles on. In C major, C is home. Call it home, or 1.
step_1_story_hook.visual: C highlighted on the keyboard as home base. The number 1 appears above it. All other notes are dim.
step_1_story_hook.audio: play C4 three times — once alone, once after a short ascending run, once after a descending run. Each time it lands, Motesart says: 'There. That's home.'

step_2_hear_it.name: Hear It
step_2_hear_it.description: Student hears the concept before they see any symbols or terminology. Audio plays. No labels on screen yet.
step_2_hear_it.motesart_intro: Listen to this. (plays ascending C major scale) Did you hear where it wanted to land at the end? That last note — that's home. That's 1.

audio_sequence.text: Hear how it settles there? That last note is home.

step_2_hear_it.visual: Scale notes light up one at a time as they play. C5 at the end glows brighter and stays lit. No W/H labels. No letter names yet — only the number 1 over the final note.

step_3_say_it.name: Say It
step_3_say_it.description: Call and response. Motesart speaks a partial phrase. Student completes it. Both voice and text input accepted.

rounds.motesart_wrong: That's what we're learning. 1 is home — say it back.

rounds.motesart_prompt: In C major, the home note is...
rounds.motesart_correct: C. That's home in C major.
rounds.motesart_wrong: In C major, home is C. Say it back — the home note is...

rounds.motesart_prompt: Home is where the music wants to...
rounds.motesart_wrong: Think about how it felt at the end of the scale. The music wants to come back home.

step_4_feel_check.name: Feel Check
step_4_feel_check.description: Audiation test. Student hears two options and chooses which one feels like home. This is NOT a graded quiz. It calibrates confidence_score internally. Student never sees Feel Check results or percentages.
step_4_feel_check.student_facing_intro: Close your eyes. I'll play two notes. After each one, just say which one felt more like home — first or second. Don't think about it. Just feel it.

step_5_name_it.name: Name It
step_5_name_it.description: Music-world name is revealed only after the student has heard, felt, and said the concept. Per Article IV of the Constitution — earned-name doctrine.
step_5_name_it.motesart_reveal: You already know what home is. Now here's the music-world name for it. Musicians call 1 the tonic — or the root. Same idea. Just the technical name. You can use either. Home. Tonic. Both are right.
step_5_name_it.child_version: You already know home. Here's what musicians call it — the tonic. Same thing. You just know it as home.
step_5_name_it.teen_version: The music-world name for home is tonic, or root. Same concept. Both words work.
step_5_name_it.adult_version: Music-world name: tonic, or root. You know it as 1 or home. All three mean the same thing.
step_5_name_it.visual: The word 'Home' on screen. An arrow appears. 'Tonic' fades in beside it. Both words stay visible.

locked_terms.reveal_trigger: after step_3 and step_4 both completed

step_6_quiz_it.name: Quiz It
step_6_quiz_it.description: Short retrieval questions. Motesart is absent during quiz questions per Article XII. A small indicator reads: 'Test mode — answer on your own.' Motesart reappears with feedback after each answer.

questions.motesart_wrong: Home is always 1. The first note. The tonic. Try again.

questions.prompt: In C major, which note is home?
questions.motesart_correct: C is home in C major. That's where the family lives.
questions.motesart_wrong: In C major, home is C. That's the first note — number 1.

questions.prompt: Home is where the music wants to...
questions.motesart_correct: Come back to. The music always wants to come home.
questions.motesart_wrong: Think about how the scale felt when it landed at the end. The music came back home.

questions.prompt: What is the music-world name for home?
questions.motesart_correct: Tonic. Or root. Both work. You earned that name.
questions.motesart_wrong: The music-world name for home is tonic. Or root. Say it back.

questions.prompt: If I told you the home note of a song is G, what number is G?
questions.motesart_correct: G would be 1. Home is always 1, no matter which note it is.
questions.motesart_wrong: Home is always 1. It doesn't matter which note it is. If G is home, G is 1.

step_7_explain_it.name: Explain It
step_7_explain_it.description: Ownership gate. Student explains the concept in their own words. Both voice and text accepted. Motesart absent during the answer. Returns with feedback. Per Article XV — ownership_status = owned required for mastery.
step_7_explain_it.prompt: In your own words — what does home mean in music, and why does it matter?
step_7_explain_it.motesart_correct: That is ownership. You are not just repeating it — you understand it.
step_7_explain_it.motesart_wrong: Try to say it in your own words. What does home mean to you in music? Why does that note matter?

wyl_interventions.description: WYL fires AFTER a mistake is detected — not from a student label, from the specific failure. Four modes serve the same concept in different ways. Per Constitution Article VI and UDL doctrine.

visual.child: Show C keyboard with a glowing home icon over C. Arrows from other notes pointing back to C. Caption: 'All roads lead home.'
visual.teen: Keyboard diagram with C highlighted. Short caption: 'C is 1. That's home in C major.'
visual.adult: Keyboard diagram. C labeled as '1 / Tonic / Home.' Brief.
visual.interaction: Student taps each note and hears Motesart say 'skip' or 'not home' until they land on C and hear 'Home.'

auditory.child: Motesart plays three short phrases. First two land away from home. Third lands on C. 'Did you hear the difference? The last one settled. That's home.'
auditory.teen: Play two endings — one resolves to C, one ends on G. 'Which one settled? Which one felt done?'
auditory.adult: Play V-I resolution (G → C). 'Hear it pull to C? That settling feeling — that's the tonic.'
auditory.interaction: Student selects 'first' or 'second' after each pair.

kinesthetic.child: Tap home button rhythm game. Motesart plays a melody. Student taps BIG when they hear it land home. 'Every time it feels done — tap!'
kinesthetic.teen: Same tap game, no BIG/SMALL language. 'Tap when you hear home.'
kinesthetic.adult: Same tap game, no scaffolding. Student taps when V-I resolution occurs.
kinesthetic.interaction: 3 rounds, each ending on C. Student taps when they feel home.

readwrite.child: Fill in: '1 is called ___. In C major, the home note is ___. Home is where the music wants to ___.'
readwrite.teen: Fill in: '1 is called home, or the ___. The home note of C major is ___.'
readwrite.adult: Fill in: 'The tonic of C major is ___. The tonic is scale degree number ___.'

categories.description: Student identifies a note other than C as home in C major
categories.trigger: answer to G0_Q2 is not C
categories.next_action: trigger WYL visual — keyboard with C highlighted as home

categories.description: Student defines home as a technique or dynamic rather than a tonal center
categories.next_action: trigger WYL auditory — hear C as the settling note

categories.description: Student cannot identify which note is 1 in a new context
categories.next_action: re-teach: home is always 1, regardless of which note

categories.description: Student confuses tonic with dominant, root with bass note, or other technical terms
categories.next_action: Motesart: 'The music-world name for home is tonic. Same idea as home. Not the chord name — just the note name.'

categories.description: Student passes G0_Q1-Q5 but cannot explain home in own words at G0_Q7
categories.trigger: is_ownership_gate passes quiz but ownership explanation fails
categories.next_action: flag as execution_only — ownership gate not passed — require retry or teacher review

mastery_rule.execution_definition: Student answers G0_Q1 through G0_Q5 with score >= 0.85
mastery_rule.ownership_definition: Student explains home in own words with at least one acceptable signal present

not_ready.motesart_response: Let's back up. We need more time here before we move on.

developing.motesart_response: You're getting there. Let's try that again.

almost_owned.motesart_response: You almost had it. One more pass and it'll stick.

mastered.motesart_response: That is locked. You know where home is.

homework_game.description: Student hears C major scale, then hears one note. They tap which key is home (1). Level 1 only — one note, one octave, C major only.
